meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).

話題.gloss: hot topic, talk of the town

meanings.en: hot topic, talk of the town

examples.text: 監督の作品、話題になってるんですね。
examples.trans: The director's new films have become the talk of the town, haven't they.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Expresses change of state, or in polite customer service (になります) states an arrangement or price total.

examples.trans: That comes to one thousand yen.

examples.text: 俺も金なんとか集めるからよ。もうちょっと明るくやろうや。
examples.trans: I'll scrape together some money too, so let's keep our spirits up.

examples.text: ああ。リスクもあるが、懸けてみるか、トシ。
examples.trans: Yeah. There's risk involved too, though—ready to take the gamble, Toshi?

examples.text: 強制送還の金がかかるだけで、何の見せしめにもならないだろ？
examples.trans: Deporting them just costs money and doesn't serve as an example to anyone, right?

meanings.note: After なくて (隠さなくて結構です), politely says 'there is no need to'.

examples.text: 明日は来なくて結構です。
examples.trans: You do not need to come tomorrow.

meanings.note: Intransitive verb describing goods selling on the market without naming a seller.

examples.text: この絵本はよく売れます。
新しい本がたくさん売れました。
examples.trans: Many copies of the new book sold.

meanings.note: Auxiliary na-adjective expressing resemblance or conjecture.

examples.trans: It looks like it's going to rain.

examples.text: 彼は忙しいみたいですね。

meanings.note: Casual counterpart of こちら.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.

examples.text: うん、結構売れてるみたい。こっちはヘトヘトだけど。
examples.trans: Yeah, they seem to be selling really well, though we are exhausted.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Limits the preceding noun or phrase to that item alone.

examples.text: これだけお願いします。

meanings.note: Used with の to modify the following noun (次のお二人様, 次の駅).

examples.trans: I get off at the next station.

meanings.note: Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.
Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

meanings.en: in that way; that is so
meanings.note: そうですか ('Is that so? / I see') calmly acknowledges news.

examples.text: そうですか、わかりました。

meanings.note: Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.

meanings.en: short casual form of じゃあ / では
meanings.note: Brisk spoken transition before taking the next step.

meanings.en: exist; be available; remain in place
meanings.note: Used for inanimate things and abstract concepts; after て-form (書いてある, 置いてある) describes a resulting state left in place.

examples.text: 名前が書いてあります。

meanings.note: Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

meanings.note: Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
Standalone casual thanks; followed by ございます (present) or ございました (completed occasion) for polite thanks.

examples.text: ありがとうございます。

meanings.en: polite auxiliary in ありがとうございます
meanings.note: Survives in modern speech chiefly in ございます (present) and ございました (past) after ありがとう and おめでとう.

examples.text: ありがとうございます。
ありがとうございました。
examples.trans: Thank you very much (for what just concluded).

meanings.note: Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.
